messages:
alex: Heads-up: noticed a regression on short-context (<=64) p95 after yesterday's kernel-autotune rollout. Looks like prefill paths are choosing the new fused-attn kernel even for tiny sequences.
priya: ugh. any numbers?
alex: p50/p95 for short ctx (prod traffic, n=12k):
```
old (baseline): p50=18ms p95=42ms
new-autotune: p50=16ms p95=78ms  <-- p95 doubled
kernel picks (sample): prefill= fused_attn_v2, decode=kv_streamed
```
mateo: interesting that p50 improved slightly but p95 jumped. suggests tail issue when fused_attn hits certain sequence shapes or batch combos.
jin: did autotune change the sequence-length bucketing thresholds?
alex: yes — autotune tightened buckets to favor fused_attn for seq_len <= 128 to save cost. That worked for medium traffic but on small bursts we see contention.
sara: can you paste the autotune config that rolled?
alex: here: 
```json
{ "autotune_version": "3.1.4", "bucket_thresholds": [16, 32, 64, 128, 256], "path_prefill": {"prefer": ["fused_attn_v2","matmul_opt"]}, "safety_fallback": true }
```
priya: safety_fallback=true should have prevented regressions if kernel latency > baseline, right?
mateo: safety_fallback is only evaluated at profiling intervals (1h). if transient tail events happen between checks it won't flip. also we saw a telemetry sampling bug that undercounts 99th during high QPS.
perf-bot: alert: short-ctx p95 spike detected (1876543210 -> 1876543290), source=runtime/autotune, delta=+36ms
jin: can we force prefill to use matmul_opt for seq<=64 on next deploy while we dig in?
alex: I tested a hotfix on staging: forcing prefill kernel to matmul_opt for <=64 brought p95 back to 44ms. patch diff: 
```diff
- prefer: ["fused_attn_v2","matmul_opt"]
+ prefer: ["matmul_opt","fused_attn_v2"]
```
sara: good quick mitigation. we should also add an eval that measures tail when mixing batch sizes. current autotune objective optimizes average cost not tail latency.
mateo: Agreed. Proposed changes:
- add tail-aware objective for buckets with seq<=128 (optimize p95 with penalty factor)
- reduce autotune sample window to 5m for prefill path changes
- add runtime guard: if p95 > baseline*1.5 within 10m, revert kernel pick immediately
priya: +1. Also add KV cache interaction test: prefill using fused_attn appears to mangle KV cache eviction patterns for small prompts, causing more KV thrashing. Need a microbenchmark.
alex: I ran a profile: KV miss rate for short ctx jumped from 2.1% -> 6.8% under fused_attn path. snippet: 
```
KV_CACHE_STATS { hits: 9819, misses: 713, miss_rate: 0.068 }
previous { hits: 9952, misses: 215, miss_rate: 0.021 }
```
jin: that explains tail. more misses => more memory ops and stalls. maybe fused_attn layout changes alignment so cache lines less reused.
sara: assign owners and next steps:
- mateo: run microbench comparing fused_attn vs matmul_opt for small seqs w/ KV enabled (include different batch mixes)
- jin: prepare quick config rollback to matmul_opt prioritization + deploy canary to 10%
- priya: add tail-aware objective and reduce sampling window in autotune service; update unit tests and eval harness
- alex: collect more traces and attach perf profiles to the ticket (use pprof + nvprof)
perf-bot: created ticket: RUNTIME-1198 (autotune-tail-regression) by perf-bot
alex: I'll attach the flamegraph I captured for one slow request: it shows long CUDA memcpy stalls during prefill KV writes. will upload in a bit.
mateo: if memcpy is the hotspot, maybe our fused kernel triggers extra host<->device movement for small batches. check kernel launch flags and whether we disable async copies for small sizes.
priya: also check batching heuristics: autotune might be grouping a small seq with a long seq in same batch and fused_attn doesn't handle mixed-length as efficiently. add a batch-mix filter in prefill path.
jin: I'll spin up a canary with the matmul_opt-first config and reduced sample window. target 10% traffic in 30m.
sara: timeline: can we have canary + initial rollback today, microbench results by EOD tomorrow, autotune change in 48h?
alex: doable. I'll pin logs to RUNTIME-1198. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
priya: thanks — good catch. one last ask: add a short note to eng-runtime channel when canary goes live so oncall watches latency dashboards.
perf-bot: canary deployed to 10% (1876543290). monitoring: p95 baseline feed enabled.
jin: noted, will post update in eng-runtime when stable.
